saml.description: SAML broker does not validate the Issuer of received assertions when Identity Provider Entity ID is empty.
saml.note: Acceptance of an assertion with an unexpected Issuer is by configuration when idpEntityId is unset; do not flag as a bug unless issuer validation was configured.

saml.description: After successful identity-provider login, the browser authentication flow does not continue unless a Post Login Flow is configured.
saml.note: SAML login succeeding without local MFA is by design if no post broker login flow enforces MFA.

saml.description: First broker login behavior may create a new user, prompt to link an existing account, or automatically link depending on the configured first login flow.
saml.note: Identity merges during first login can be expected behavior under the selected flow and should not be treated as collisions without flow-aware analysis.

saml.description: Usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case; case-sensitive username only preserves the original federated username metadata.
saml.note: Case-only differences may normalize in local usernames and should not automatically be flagged as identity collapse.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, email addresses from the identity provider are trusted and may be marked verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode.
saml.note: Email-based linking or verified-email state changes may be by design under trusted-email configuration.

saml.description: Users created or imported through identity brokering can automatically receive default roles and default groups.
saml.note: Extra downstream permissions may come from realm policy, not from over-acceptance of upstream SAML assertions.

saml.description: When using metadata descriptor URL for SAML trust, validating certificates are cached and refreshed according to metadata/cache provider rules.
saml.note: Temporary acceptance of old signing keys before cache refresh is expected caching behavior.

saml.description: When validating external provider signatures via metadata/JWKS URLs, Keycloak caches keys and may continue using cached keys until refresh conditions are met.
saml.note: Temporary acceptance of old signing keys before cache refresh is expected caching behavior.

saml.description: When an administrator updates SAML provider certificates, metadata URL, or issuer settings, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
saml.note: Do not flag successful login after admin-authorized trust-anchor change as a vulnerability.

saml.constraint: For I1 SAML signature-validation tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing hardened configurations. The documentation states that Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether a signed Assertion is expected. If these are left unset in a default-config test, successful login may reflect insecure defaults rather than a bypass of an enabled check.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, config.identity_provider_entity_id is the trust anchor for SAML Issuer validation. If this field is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Therefore, when testing saml_issuer_mismatch, the fuzzer MUST run both: (a) a default-config test with idpEntityId unset to detect skipped validation by default, and (b) an enforcement test with config.identity_provider_entity_id set to the expected IdP entity ID. Without setting this field, issuer-mismatch acceptance is by configuration, not necessarily a bug.

For I1 trust-anchor tests involving metadata/JWKS-like certificate refresh, config.use_metadata_descriptor_url causes Keycloak to download and cache IdP certificates from config.metadata_descriptor_url. Old certificates may remain accepted until cache refresh rules based on descriptor cacheDuration/validUntil or cache provider limits. Do NOT flag acceptance of an old signing cert before cache expiry as a trust-anchor violation; only flag if acceptance persists after cache refresh should have occurred.

For I1 SAML certificate-substitution tests, if config.use_metadata_descriptor_url=false then signature validation uses config.validating_x509_certificates only. If config.use_metadata_descriptor_url=true, certificates are refreshed from metadata and may change independently of static config. The fuzzer MUST choose one trust mode per test and not mix expectations across them.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertion replay and OneTimeUse replay are the relevant freshness checks. Do NOT apply JWT bearer replay expectations here. The attack sequence for SAML must reuse the same Assertion/@ID via fixed_assertion_id and, for OneTimeUse, include include_onetimeuse=true on both submissions.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control saml_login without expired_assertion=true before the attack saml_login with expired_assertion=true. Otherwise, a failed expired assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken IdP/SP setup.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, Keycloak documentation states that browser authentication flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login unless a Post Login Flow is configured. Therefore, to test whether SAML login bypasses MFA, the realm/IdP MUST have a post-login flow that enforces OTP or other MFA after broker login. If no post-login flow is configured, successful SAML login without MFA is by design and not evidence of bypass.

For I4 account-linking tests, automatic linking of existing accounts is potentially dangerous and depends on the configured First Login Flow. The default first broker login flow may prompt for confirmation, email verification, or re-authentication; alternative flows such as Automatically Set Existing User can auto-link without verification. The fuzzer MUST record which first_login_flow_alias is configured and MUST NOT treat account linking as a collision unless the configured flow should have prevented it.

For I4 email-based takeover tests, config.trust_email only marks brokered email as verified and can affect linking/import behavior on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode. If trust_email=true and the first login flow permits automatic linking, email-based merges may be configuration-driven. The fuzzer MUST test both trust_email=false and trust_email=true scenarios when evaluating unverified_email_account_linking or saml_email_binding_collision.

For I4 username comparison tests, Keycloak usernames in the server are always lower-case, while the identity provider setting Case-sensitive username only affects the federated identity username associated with the brokered identity. Therefore, case-only differences in upstream identity may normalize in local usernames. The oracle MUST not treat lowercasing alone as a collision without checking the underlying broker identity/session claims.

For I5 audience/conditions tests on SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between missing Conditions, wrong Audience, and missing AudienceRestriction. The docs describe assertion Conditions and AudienceRestriction in successful SAML responses and client assertion lifespan settings, but broker acceptance behavior depends on signature/issuer/audience configuration. Use separate tests: remove_conditions=true for no Conditions, wrong audience mutation for AudienceRestriction mismatch, and baseline control login for comparison.

For I5 authorization-binding tests involving roles/groups after broker login, Keycloak may add default roles and default groups automatically to users created or imported through identity brokering. Therefore, permissions observed after SAML login may exceed upstream assertion content because of realm default role/group assignment by policy, which is by configuration. The fuzzer MUST account for realm default roles/groups before flagging privilege escalation.

For I5 scope/role tests against downstream tokens, role scope mappings limit roles included in issued tokens/assertions to the intersection of user roles and client role-scope mappings. A missing role in the downstream token may be due to client scope configuration rather than failed identity import. The fuzzer MUST verify client role-scope mappings before interpreting missing permissions as identity or authorization bugs.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, which defaults to 30 minutes. SAML broker flows are session-bound; the executor must initiate the SP flow and submit the SAMLResponse within the same live authentication session. Reusing an old RelayState/InResponseTo after timeout will fail for session reasons, not necessarily because of security enforcement.

The browser may automatically restart authentication in other tabs after one tab completes login because authentication sub-sessions share a root authentication session. For I3 flow-coherence tests, do not use multi-tab/browser-side behavior as evidence of session confusion; show inconsistent handling of the same request within one intended flow instead.

If organizations are enabled in the realm, the browser and first broker login flows are modified to support identity-first login and organization onboarding. This can automatically redirect users to organization-linked identity providers based on email domain. SAML broker tests in such realms MUST control organization configuration, otherwise redirects/account assignment may be organization behavior rather than generic broker behavior.

For I1 SAML signature-substitution tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing hardened configurations. The documentation states that Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether a signed Assertion is expected. If these are omitted or left OFF, acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned assertions may be due to permissive configuration rather than a verification flaw.

For I1 SAML issuer-validation tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST set config.idpEntityId. The documentation explicitly says: if Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Therefore, a saml_issuer_mismatch test is only meaningful when idpEntityId is configured; otherwise acceptance of a wrong Issuer is by configuration.

For I1 trust-anchor rotation and certificate-substitution tests with config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=true, account for certificate caching. The documentation states certificates are downloaded from Metadata descriptor URL and cached; refresh behavior differs for POST vs REDIRECT binding and may depend on descriptor cacheDuration/validUntil or cache provider defaults. Do NOT flag temporary acceptance of old keys before cache refresh/expiry as a vulnerability.

For I1 tests using static certificates, if config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=false then signature validation uses config.signingCertificate. To test attacker-cert rejection correctly, the fuzzer MUST ensure the configured validating certificate set does not include the attacker certificate and MUST save the provider after any imported-key change.

For I2 SAML replay tests, use saml_login against the broker endpoint only after initiating the SP flow. The ACS endpoint requires SP-initiated flow state and matching InResponseTo; the executor must honor metadata.initiate_saml_flow=true. Otherwise replay or freshness failures may be caused by missing flow state rather than assertion validation.

For I2 assertion-expiry tests, include a control saml_login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion. Without a control, rejection of expired_assertion=true cannot be distinguished from broken IdP/provider setup or missing SP-initiated flow state.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, configure the SAML provider's Post Login Flow to enforce MFA after broker login. The documentation states browser flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login and additional steps such as 2FA require a Post login flow. Therefore, absence of MFA after SAML login is not evidence of bypass unless Post Login Flow is configured to require MFA.

For I4 account-linking and email-collision tests, Trust Email MUST be treated as security-sensitive. When Trust Email is ON, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on first and subsequent logins depending on sync mode. Tests for unverified_email_account_linking or email-based takeover MUST disable trustEmail unless the test explicitly targets trusted-email behavior.

For I4 username/case tests, account for config.caseSensitiveOriginalUsername semantics. The documentation states usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case; this setting only affects the username associated with the federated identity. Therefore, verify_granted_identity may return lower-cased usernames even when the upstream identity used mixed case. Do not treat lowercasing alone as a collision unless distinct upstream identities collapse to the same downstream account.

For I4 principal-binding tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST choose principal extraction deliberately. config.principalType can use Subject NameID or a SAML attribute, and config.principalAttribute selects the identifying attribute. Different settings change which upstream field binds the account. Multi-identity tests must hold this constant; otherwise identity merges/splits may be caused by configuration changes rather than broker flaws.

For I5 audience/conditions tests on SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST distinguish broker-as-SP validation from downstream client validation. The SAML IdP broker documentation exposes issuer/signature settings but does not document a broker-side toggle for requiring AudienceRestriction or Conditions on inbound assertions. Therefore, acceptance of assertions without Conditions or with wrong Audience should be tested empirically and interpreted carefully, with a valid-control login in the same provider configuration.

For I5 authorization-binding tests involving roles/groups after SAML login, remember that default roles and default groups are automatically assigned to users created or imported through identity brokering. Access granted solely because of realm default roles/groups is by design and must not be misclassified as upstream-assertion privilege escalation.

For organization-linked IdPs, Advanced Claim to Group mapper claim values support two modes: exact match by default, or regex when Regex Claim Values is enabled. For multi-identity I4 tests, if multiple different values must pass the same mapper, the fuzzer MUST either omit the mapper or explicitly enable regex mode with an appropriate pattern. Do NOT assume wildcard semantics in exact mode.

For RequestedAuthnContext testing, config.authnContextComparisonType has enumerated semantics Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better; default is Exact. The fuzzer MUST set the intended comparison explicitly when testing step-up or MFA-related behavior, because leaving it unset changes matching semantics and can cause false positives.

For default-config insecure-default testing of saml_cert_substitution, the fuzzer MUST create the SAML IdP with default/minimal config and MUST NOT set config.validateSignature=true or config.wantAssertionsSigned=true. The attack specifically tests whether Keycloak accepts attacker-signed SAML responses under default settings.

Identity Provider Entity ID matching is exact string validation of the SAML Issuer. The documentation says 'If empty, no Issuer validation is performed.' There is no companion match-mode parameter. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure config.idpEntityId to the trusted issuer value. For multi-identity scenarios, do NOT try to use wildcards; omit the field only if you intentionally want issuer validation disabled.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, if config.idpEntityId is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation. A login accepted with an untrusted Issuer under that configuration is by setup, not necessarily a bug. The fuzzer MUST run both a configured-issuer test and, separately, an insecure-default test if desired.

When config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=true, SAML signature validation keys are downloaded and cached from the metadata descriptor URL. Old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh conditions are met, especially for REDIRECT binding where refresh happens only after max cache time. For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests, do NOT flag acceptance of old signing keys before metadata/JWKS cache expiry.

For I1/I3 trust-anchor tests using static certificates, set config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl=false and provide config.signingCertificate explicitly. Otherwise metadata-driven key refresh and cache behavior can mask whether the configured trust anchor actually changed.

SAML broker login is browser-flow/session-bound. The ACS endpoint /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/endpoint expects a response correlated to an SP-initiated flow. The executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo context; otherwise failures are flow-setup errors, not security rejections. This is required for valid I3 flow-coherence testing.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, which defaults to 30 minutes. Multi-step SAML broker tests must complete within the authentication-session lifetime or re-initiate the flow. Expired authentication sessions can cause protocol-specific errors that are not security failures.

The authenticationSessions SPI parameter authSessionsLimit has numeric sentinel semantics: value 300 is the documented default maximum number of AuthenticationSessionEntity per RootAuthenticationSessionEntity; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed on new authentication requests. This is not a token-use budget but it can evict parallel browser-tab auth state. Do not run large parallel SAML login attempts in one browser context without accounting for this cap.

For I2 SAML replay tests (saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay), include a control login first with a fresh assertion to confirm the provider and flow work. A failed replay attempt is only meaningful if the same configuration accepts a valid non-replayed assertion.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control login without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Otherwise a rejection cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup, missing flow state, or unrelated SAML validation failure.

For I4 identity-binding tests, Keycloak may lowercase brokered usernames unless 'Case-sensitive username' is enabled. The documentation states that when disabled, the username from the identity provider is lower-cased, while usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. Therefore case-only differences in granted identity may be normalization, not collision. Use the provider setting deliberately when testing case_confusion.

For I4 account-linking and email-collision tests, Trust Email materially changes linking risk. When trustEmail is ON, brokered emails may be treated as verified and can affect first-login/account-linking behavior. Tests for unverified_email_account_linking or saml_email_binding_collision MUST control trustEmail and firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias; otherwise automatic linking behavior may be by configuration.

The default first broker login flow can create a new user if unique, or attempt linking when email/username matches an existing account. This means same-email broker logins may merge or prompt for linking by design. For I4 principal-binding tests, distinguish between configured first-login linking behavior and unintended identity collapse.

The 'Automatically Set Existing User' authenticator in a custom first login flow is explicitly documented as dangerous because it links existing users without verification. If a test realm uses such a flow, account takeover/linking results are by design and MUST NOT be reported as product vulnerabilities.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule, MFA enforcement after broker login depends on the configured Post Login Flow. The documentation states that browser flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login and additional steps like 2FA require a post broker login flow. Therefore, to test MFA bypass correctly, the fuzzer MUST configure postBrokerLoginFlowAlias to a flow that enforces OTP/MFA after SAML login; otherwise SAML login without MFA is expected behavior.

For SAML client-side authorization binding tests, remember that SAML client role/organization/group claims in assertions are shaped by client scopes and role scope mappings. By default, clients may receive all user role mappings unless Full Scope Allowed is turned off or scope mappings are narrowed. Apparent over-grant in downstream SAML assertions can be default client configuration rather than broker escalation.

For organization-group mapping tests on SAML clients, organization groups are automatically included through the built-in saml_organization scope only when the Organization Membership mapper and Organization Group Membership mapper are present in the same scope. Missing group claims may be mapper configuration, not authorization denial.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
